summary: 9remote exposes installer host shell to the public internet via Cloudflare Quick Tunnel
details: The package spawns a local PTY (bash/zsh/cmd/powershell via ptyDaemon.cjs) and runs an HTTP/WebSocket server (server.cjs) that publishes itself to the public internet through a trycloudflare.com Quick Tunnel. Incoming WebSocket `input` messages are written directly into the spawned shell (`case "input":... b.pty.write(s.data)`), giving anyone who reaches the tunnel URL and passes the pairing check full interactive command execution on the host running the tool. server.cjs routes non-loopback requests bearing `cf-connecting-ip` into the same session/PTY control plane, and dist/cli.cjs issues POST traffic to the tunnel control endpoints. The tool is invoked by the operator via its bin entry rather than at install/require time, so consumer intent is present, but the resulting exposure is a full-host remote shell reachable from the public internet, gated only by a pairing secret and Cloudflare's ephemeral tunnel URL.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
